description:
🔥 Become an AI engineer: https://www.skool.com/aiengineer/about
🗄️ Let's connect on Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/_owainlewis/

👋🏼 If you're new, I'm Owain. I've been building software for 20 years as a principal AI engineer and engineering director. I run my own AI consultancy, building custom software for business owners.

GPT-6 Astra is OpenAI's latest model, and its computer use is the feature I care about most. I used it with Codex to build Vertica, a custom app that turns a headline and a few tips into finished Instagram and LinkedIn carousels in minutes.

In this video, I walk through Vertica and the workflow around it, including the carousel editor and layouts, image and video backgrounds, SVG diagrams inside slides, JPEG, PDF and video export, Codex driving the app through Browser Use, and generating a video background with Higgsfield. I also show Codex building a full carousel about GPT-6 from the OpenAI benchmark page without me touching the browser.

Agents in a terminal are fine for one-off tasks, but for repeatable work like posting to social media they get slow, skills get lost, and I get distracted. I still use Codex for most of my development, but for the actual posting workflow I'd rather have software I log into and let the agent operate it. Custom software + browser use beats a terminal for this kind of work IMO.

What you'll learn:

- Why I built Vertica instead of writing another agent skill
- The two ways to run Browser Use in OpenAI Codex
- How Codex pulled GPT-6 benchmarks from the OpenAI site and turned them into slides
- Generating a video background with Higgsfield and uploading it through the browser
Deploying to Google Cloud with object storage and FFmpeg for text overlays on MP4
What I actually think of GPT-6 Astra day to day, and why I've stopped trusting benchmarks

🔗 Links
Vertica source code: https://github.com/owainlewis/vertica
Training for ambitious software builders: https://aiengineer.co
Let's connect on Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/_owainlewis/

Drop a comment with any topics you'd like me to cover in future videos.
